rationale: A wins because it keeps the sharpest accountability stories closer to the supplied facts instead of freelancing a market thesis. A's "REI won't say how big its resale business actually is" is a clean, reportable tension with the missing proof named; B's "a public retailer answering to shareholders has a hard time cheering on resale, which cannibalizes new-product margin" smuggles in a whole business-school essay the update never supplied. B has the better store-labor questions, but that grounding slip is exactly how a founder gets pantsed on a reporter call.
gaps_in_A: "REI's bet: gear resale and repair aren't a sustainability side project, they're core retail infrastructure" overclaims from one retailer rollout; the set admits it still needs comparative data before making that category claim.

"the dividend flows to paying customer-members, not to the employees organizing" is too clean. The update says member dividend and unionization activity; it does not prove how employee membership, benefits, or compensation intersect.

"What REI's 'record dividend' actually means when the company has no shareholders" compresses "not publicly traded" into "no shareholders." For a co-op, that wording needs tightening or it invites a pedant with a deadline.
The retail-ops angle and the "core retail infrastructure" angle share too much oxygen unless the comparative proof appears. Without it, the fourth angle is a trend wrapper on the first.
gaps_in_B: "a public retailer answering to shareholders has a hard time cheering on resale, which cannibalizes new-product margin" is an invented premise. No margin data, competitor comparison, or public-retailer evidence was supplied.

"every store needs intake space, grading standards, technicians, and inventory handling" states implementation details the facts do not establish. Those belong as reporting questions, not assumptions.

"Trade-in counters and repair benches arrive at REI stores" may be physically false. The update says repairs are available at stores; it does not say every store has a bench, technician, or full-service repair operation.

"a reporter who has been chasing the same non-disclosure across apparel and outdoor brands" invents a reporter context and broader industry pattern. Keep the angle on REI unless you have outside evidence.
